name: LimeHippo Payments and Installments (UA)
author: LimeHippo

sections.description:
Free connects a WooCommerce store to Ukrainian payment services. Create a separate connection for each merchant account and choose a name that buyers will see at checkout.

Included in Free

  • Bank transfer with IBAN and QR. On a live HTTPS store, buyers can copy the recipient details or download a QR code for the exact UAH order amount. After checking the bank statement, the merchant confirms receipt in WooCommerce.
  • LiqPay and plata by mono card payments. Buyers can pay on the provider’s hosted page. The store can check payment status, offer another attempt after a confirmed refusal and record confirmed refunds against the order. On a production store enable a live merchant connection.
  • Wallets on the provider’s page. A wallet offered by the bank on its own payment page is part of that provider’s checkout. Its availability depends on the bank, merchant account and buyer’s device.

What the separate Pro add-on adds

  • Wallets at the WooCommerce checkout. Buyers can select Apple Pay or Google Pay before leaving the store. Each wallet uses a configured LiqPay or mono merchant connection. Separate mono wallets need Google Pay production access or Apple merchant certificates and domain verification.
  • Installments. Configure PrivatBank Payment in Parts, PrivatBank Instant Installments and mono Purchase in Parts. Choose eligible categories, products and variations, display the payment count on catalog cards and manage applications from the order.

Free runs independently. Pro requires Free and is distributed separately by LimeHippo.

Order status and recovery

The order page checks the store’s transfer status while it is open and when
the buyer returns to the tab. It removes the IBAN, QR and banking link once
the store confirms receipt, the order is cancelled or the transfer needs review.

On failed card and wallet orders, Classic checkout, Checkout Blocks and My Account
offer another payment when the store can safely accept it. An older order payment
link leads to the payment status while the bank is processing the transaction.

Buyers can cancel an unpaid order before payment starts. While a bank payment
or installment application is outstanding, WooCommerce checks cancellation
links against its current status. After a final refusal, the store checks
the previous payment before allowing the buyer to cancel the order.

Merchant setup

Use HTTPS, UAH and a merchant account approved by the bank. Create a connection in WooCommerce, select the live environment and enter the credentials for this store. LiqPay requires the public and private key from the same merchant account. For mono, use the acquiring token issued for real transactions. Use sandbox credentials only on a development or staging copy. A successful mono connection check verifies API access; the bank determines the token environment.
For IBAN transfers, confirm receipt manually after reconciling the order with your statement.

After saving a token, use Check connection to confirm mono API access. A replacement
token must belong to the same merchant; use a new connection for another merchant.
Changing only a label preserves verification. Temporary API outages preserve a prior
successful check for unchanged credentials. Rejected tokens disable new checkout.
Repeated merchant connections produce an informational warning and remain supported.

If checkout stops while replacing a refused LiqPay payment or a closed mono invoice,
the buyer can resume the same order from its details. The plugin checks the previous
attempt before issuing a replacement. A conflicting transaction, payment date or
refund blocks another charge and shows the buyer how to contact the store.

The order confirmation and account pages check the shop’s saved payment status while
a mono or LiqPay payment is pending. When the result or retry eligibility changes,
the page refreshes. A customer status check does not contact the bank.

Order details show the amount refunded against the original mono or LiqPay payment,
including supported LiqPay and mono wallet payments. Pending and declined refunds have their own messages.
If the bank result and the WooCommerce refund record disagree, the buyer is referred
to the store for confirmation.

Implemented: invoice creation and redirect, signed callbacks, authenticated status reconciliation,
guest return checks, background reconciliation, WooCommerce payment completion, transaction IDs,
idempotent replay handling and retries after confirmed invoice invalidation. Orders and stock
use WooCommerce CRUD APIs. MySQL/MariaDB advisory locks serialize payment completion.
If mono reports payment on an invalidated invoice, the order requires reconciliation.
Checkout and refunds stay blocked across its payment attempts. An interrupted retry
checks the original invoice and order details before issuing a replacement link.

Each attempt retains its account, amount, currency and encrypted token snapshot. An uncertain
invoice creation is never retried automatically. Unknown outcomes and conflicting paid orders
require manual bank/order review. The order action requests a fresh provider status check.
Background jobs use Action Scheduler or WP-Cron. Working scheduled tasks are required.

Once payment starts, the order is detached from WooCommerce’s mutable cart draft.
Repeated checkout for the same cart links to the existing order instead of rewriting
its method or items. Explicitly clearing the cart permits a later identical purchase.
LiqPay diagnostics show the last status check and the first confirmation source for
new payments. Only safe result codes are stored; unsigned callbacks cannot change them.

Amount-only partial and full refunds are available in the order’s mono refund panel.
For a LiqPay card payment, you can issue a full refund, or a partial refund followed
by one refund of the entire remaining balance. A LiqPay wallet payment supports one refund
operation. mono wallet payments support partial refunds and refunds of the remaining balance.
Each request is sent once. The plugin waits for an authenticated status or signed callback
with status reversed and the matching cumulative refund_amount. WooCommerce records each
confirmed refund separately. A partial refund keeps the order paid.
Pending or uncertain operations block further requests; only matching authenticated bank
confirmation creates a WooCommerce refund. Stock restocking and fiscal returns are separate.
The standard WooCommerce automatic-refund button is not used for this asynchronous flow.
Bank-dashboard refunds or conflicting manual Woo refunds require review and are not imported.

Supported card refunds use amounts. Reconcile inventory and fiscal receipts separately. Installment checkout requires Pro.
A new LiqPay attempt is allowed only after the old
signed form expires (one hour plus five minutes of local grace) and a fresh status request
confirms failure/error. Expiry, timeout or payment_not_found alone cannot authorize retry.
The old attempt and credentials remain in the journal. An authenticated conflicting old
success blocks the current handoff and automatic order completion. Retiring an attempt
is a local operation, never a claim that the bank deleted the old payment.
The mono sandbox does not offer Apple Pay/Google Pay.

Existing Delivery and Receipts automation can consume woocommerce_payment_complete.
This plugin does not issue a duplicate fiscal receipt or refund when a parcel is returned.

External services

monobank (Universal Bank)

When an administrator selects Check connection, the saved token is sent in an HTTPS
header to https://api.monobank.ua/api/merchant/details. This read-only request retrieves
the merchant name and identifier; it does not create an invoice or confirm wallet access.
When a customer selects an enabled mono method, this plugin sends the amount, UAH currency,
random payment reference, return URL and callback URL to https://api.monobank.ua/ using the
configured token. No card details are collected by the plugin. The customer enters card data
on the bank-hosted page at https://pay.monobank.ua/ or https://pay.mbnk.biz/.
The plugin requests public signing keys and invoice statuses, and invalidates failed
invoices before a new attempt. Signed callbacks are received at its REST endpoint.
An authorized administrator can request a refund; its invoice ID, integer amount
and random cancellation reference are sent to mono with the original merchant token.
Documentation: https://monobank.ua/api-docs/acquiring
Testing: https://monobank.ua/api-docs/acquiring/dev/test/docs–testing
Service provider: Universal Bank / monobank, https://monobank.ua/
Merchant terms and conditions: https://monobank.ua/terms
Privacy: https://www.universalbank.com.ua/storage/app/media/2026/documents/poryadok-ta-protsedura-zakhistu-personalnikh-danikh-v-at-universal-bank.pdf
The bank lists its current privacy document under “Порядок і процедура захисту персональних даних” at https://monobank.ua/about

LiqPay (PrivatBank)

LiqPay hosted checkout sends a signed API v7 payment form to
https://www.liqpay.ua/api/3/checkout. It contains the public key, exact amount, currency,
order reference, description, expiry, language and return/callback URLs. Dedicated Pro
wallet methods restrict paytypes to apay or gpay. The private key stays on the server.
Signed status requests and explicitly requested partial or full refunds go to
https://www.liqpay.ua/api/request. Refunds send the original purchase reference and
requested amount using the frozen payment keys. Callbacks
require SHA3-256 signature verification and matching merchant/order/amount/currency.
No PAN, CVV, card tokens or raw bank responses are stored. Use live merchant keys on a
production store and sandbox keys only on a development or staging copy.
The LiqPay page language is Ukrainian or English, as documented by the current API.
Documentation: https://www.liqpay.ua/uk/doc/api/internet_acquiring/checkout
Testing: https://www.liqpay.ua/uk/doc/api/testing
Provider: LiqPay / PrivatBank, https://www.liqpay.ua/
Merchant acquiring terms (section 3.6): https://www.liqpay.ua/information/terms
Privacy: https://privatbank.ua/personal-information

WayForPay (historical test orders)

Historical WayForPay attempts from earlier development builds retain compatibility.
WayForPay is not available for new connections or checkout. Its existing hosted form sends a signed form to https://secure.wayforpay.com/pay.
Fields include its public demonstration merchant, website domain, random reference,
order timestamp, exact UAH amount, a single order-total line, language, expiry and
return/notification URLs. No buyer email, phone, card data or merchant secret is sent.
Backend requests go only to https://api.wayforpay.com/api with CHECK_STATUS, the
merchant, reference and signature. Responses require matching signed payment fields.
The browser return only redirects to the order page and cannot confirm payment.
Callbacks are signed acknowledgements; polling is bounded and repeated events are safe.
No raw provider body, card mask, authorization code or recurring token is stored.
Documentation: https://wiki.wayforpay.com/view/852102
Status API: https://wiki.wayforpay.com/view/852117
Testing: https://wiki.wayforpay.com/view/852472
Provider: WayForPay, https://wayforpay.com/
Payment service terms: https://wayforpay.com/wfp/files/oferta.pdf
Privacy and personal data processing for Ukrainian transfers: https://wayforpay.com/wfp/files/oferta.pdf#page=9
The Ukrainian provider includes the data controller, purposes, recipients and data subject rights in the agreement and its consent annex.

Data handling

The plugin stores connection labels, environments, encrypted credentials, modification
times and editor IDs in WordPress options. Connection checks retain a merchant name,
a keyed merchant fingerprint, check times and safe result codes. Raw response bodies,
raw merchant identifiers from API responses are not stored. Bank transfer recipient names,
IBANs and tax IDs are encrypted in configuration and frozen in payment attempts.
They are displayed to the authorized customer as payment instructions. Activation creates a private payment-attempt
table. Attempts retain encrypted credential snapshots so that later account changes do
not alter historic payment bindings. Checkout and status jobs use the selected provider API.
Raw callback bodies and card data are not stored. Admin connection forms do not call the bank.
Credentials use OpenSSL AES-256-GCM with a key derived from the WordPress authentication salt.
Changing that salt without migrating credentials prevents them from being decrypted.
Encryption is not protection against full server compromise. Back up site keys and data together.

Deactivation and deletion preserve configuration and the ledger. There is no automatic data-erasure routine.
Free does not require a license. Paid features and license activation are provided by
the separate Pro add-on.

Bank transfer / QR

Multiple independent bank accounts are available in Classic and Blocks checkout.
Use a test connection on a development site. To accept transfers on an HTTPS production
store, explicitly enable a live recipient on that store. WooCommerce keeps the order
on hold until the store confirms receipt against the bank statement.
Orders wait on hold. An authorized store operator must acknowledge receipt of the full
amount to confirm payment. The plugin does not access a bank balance or statement.
Recipient details and purpose are frozen per order; later account changes do not alter them.
An order with a changed amount, currency or payment method cannot be confirmed.
If an on-hold order already has a payment date or transaction ID, the store must review it.
The order editor and customer instructions include the same reference for reconciliation.
Cancelled and paid orders do not show payable QR instructions. No automatic refunds.

NBU format 003 is generated locally with Nayuki QR Code generator 1.8.0 (MIT).
Amounts are UAH only. QR error correction is Q or M, versions 10-17, with the hryvnia
mark. Cyrillic recipient names and payment purposes use the compact Windows-1251
encoding defined by the NBU. Details too long for the QR remain available for copying.
No payment details are sent to a QR-generation service. Opening the banking-app link
visits https://qr.bank.gov.ua/ with the encoded payment instructions and requires an app
that supports this format. Scanning a QR or returning to the order never confirms payment.
No banking-app acceptance has been established by automated QR decoding tests.
Format: https://bank.gov.ua/admin_uploads/law/19082025_97.pdf
Amendment: https://bank.gov.ua/admin_uploads/law/11102025_128.pdf
QR library: https://github.com/nayuki/QR-Code-generator/tree/v1.8.0

Support and diagnostics

The Support tab includes a grouped FAQ, an optional feedback form and an explicitly
generated local configuration report. All three are available in Ukrainian, Russian
and English, with the same visual controls as Delivery and Receipts.

Submitting the form sends the entered reply email, subject, type, message and payment
plugin version to support@limehippo.com through WordPress wp_mail and the website mail
service. It never automatically attaches a site report, keys or customer/order data.
Do not include sensitive information in your message. A successful wp_mail result
means acceptance by the mail service, not confirmed delivery to the support inbox.
The form requires payment-settings permissions and a nonce. A per-user atomic lock
limits new requests to one per two minutes. Request status (without message content)
is retained for 24 hours; repeated or uncertain requests cannot send a second copy.

Preparing/copying a diagnostics report makes no bank or support request. The report
contains validated software versions, configuration flags and aggregate provider,
wallet and installment-profile counts. It excludes credentials, names, merchant and
order identifiers, customer data, site URL, phones and raw provider responses. It is
not attached to the feedback form, and does not prove bank access or scheduler health.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First stable release with LiqPay and plata by mono card payments, Ukrainian IBAN transfers and order-specific QR codes.
  • Includes Classic and Blocks checkout, payment-status reconciliation, supported refunds and safe payment retries.
  • The separate Pro add-on provides dedicated Apple Pay and Google Pay methods and PrivatBank and mono installments.

short_description: Accept UAH payments with LiqPay, plata by mono, or Ukrainian IBAN transfers with an order-specific QR code.
